title: Fixed-coefficient diagonal dualizing objects and coordinate normalization
statement: In the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], write A=P.Coefficient and N=P.diagonalExponent as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For a compactifiable scheme morphism f:X→Y define the ordinary object omega0_f=Rf^times(A_Y[0]) and the transported pro-etale object omega_f=sfFiniteExceptionalAt(f)(nu_Y^* A_Y[0]) [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The comparison-unit isomorphism at the bounded-below unit induces c_f:omega_f≈nu_X^*omega0_f. For an ordinary isomorphism e:omega0_f≈A_X(d)[2d], define coordinate normalization as follows: on every pair of separated quasi-compact etale maps j:U→X and v:U→A^d_Y with v p=j f, j^*(e inverse) followed by the source-etale exceptional locality is the finite Tate pullback comparison, followed by v^* of the actual ordered affine counit transpose and its source-etale locality. Use the equality-induced comparison for v p=j f. Quantify over every normalized twist transport, projective-line datum and compact-support normalization [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class, def-amb-vector-integration, def-pur-etale-exceptional-precomp-locality]. Define DiagonalDualizingConclusion to assert a unique theta:omega_f≈A_X(d)[2d] admitting a normalized ordinary presentation e and satisfying theta=c_f composed with nu_X^*e. All definitions here are the existing declarations extracted verbatim, not alternative notions.
